findings.issue: P123.82-64p widened _rewrite_action to a word-boundary search over the whole action, but the action is not git's alone: `git merge <branch>` writes `merge <branch>: ...` and `git pull origin <branch>` writes `pull origin <branch>: ...`, so the branch name is caller text in the action, as the commit subject was in P123.81. Measured in a scratch repo: after `git merge fix/reset-flow` the phase branch's reflog holds `merge fix/reset-flow: Merge made by the 'ort' strategy.`, and _rewrite_action returns True for it (and for `pull origin rebase-docs: Fast-forward`). branch_history then raises a history-rewrite BREACH on a linear branch, the false-breach class P123.81 closed, now reachable through branch names. rw8 pins only `prebase`/`resets` and a commit subject, never a merge or pull naming a branch.
findings.resolution: Match the verb as the action's command, not as any word in it: a rewrite verb at the start (`^(?:rebase|reset|filter-branch)\b`) or the `--rebase` flag token (`(?:^|\s)--rebase(?:=\S+)?(?:\s|$)`, which a branch name cannot spell), so `pull -q --rebase (finish)` stays a rewrite while `merge fix/reset-flow` and `pull origin rebase-docs` do not. Add rw cases for those two messages (and a merge of `rebase-x`) beside rw7/rw8.

findings.issue: drive() gives the phase lock back only when the code is E_STOPPED. The two E_USAGE returns in drive_locked (`--answer ... needs --reason`, and answer_refusal) come after take_lock and keep it, recorded as lock=taken in the state. A later next re-enters and releases it, so it is not lost, but a user who walks away after a mistyped --answer leaves phase-<id> held, which the desired outcome (a stopped drive leaves no lock behind) reads as stranded. dl2/dl3 pin only the verb-refusal stop. Reading only; not run.
findings.resolution: Decide and pin it: either release on E_USAGE when no decision is pending (state.get('pending') is None), or add a case saying the lock is deliberately kept across a refused answer because the pending decision is still this run.
